memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then Moses said to the Israelites, 'See, the Lord has chosen Bezalel son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah, and he has filled him with the Spirit of God, with wisdom, with understanding, with knowledge and with all kinds of skills.'" - Exod 35:30-31 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here is the first person in the Bible explicitly described as filled with the Spirit of God. Not a prophet. Not a priest. A craftsman.

Sit with that. The first recorded filling of the Spirit in Scripture is given to a man so that he can work with metal, stone and wood beautifully.

We have often drawn a hard line between "spiritual" work and "secular" work. Scripture draws it much less sharply. Bezalel's artistry was Spirit-empowered. His wisdom, understanding, knowledge and skill are all traced back to God as the giver.

That means your competence is not self-generated. The engineer's precision, the nurse's steadiness, the teacher's patience, the cook's instinct — every good and perfect gift is from above (Jas 1:17). We hold our abilities as stewards, not owners.

Note that Bezalel is named. In a chapter full of anonymous givers, God records this man's name and his father's and grandfather's. God knows exactly who is doing His work.

And note the tribe: Judah — the tribe from which Christ would come (Heb 7:14). Long before the King arrived, God was building His dwelling place through Judah's hands.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you see your daily skills as gifts from God's Spirit?
2. Where have you separated "spiritual" from "ordinary" work in your thinking?
3. What ability do you need to start using for God's purposes?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that every ability I have came from You. Fill me by Your Spirit and use my work for Your glory. Amen.
